# Results — Study 297 (March-Madness) on the ^GSPC daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). NCAA tournament windows
are hardcoded in [`data.py`](../march_madness/data.py) (1985-2025, 2020 cancelled).
S&P 500 daily close-to-close **price** returns (split-adjusted, no dividends) are
read from the repo-level cache `_cache/^GSPC_split_only.parquet`. Match the
fingerprint below to confirm you hold the same tape. As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n obs | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| ^GSPC daily price return (split-adjusted, no dividends) | 1985-01-02 – 2025-12-31 | 10,330 days | `2d2855ee9407` |
| NCAA tournament windows | 1985-2025 (40 brackets; 2020 cancelled) | 503 in-window trading days | hardcoded constant |

In-tournament days are **503 / 10,330 = 4.9%** of the tape — the ~3-week
Thursday-first-round-through-Monday-final stretch, 40 times over.

## Primary spec — mean daily return, in-window vs outside

| Regime | n days | mean daily | HAC t (own mean) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **In tournament** | 503 | **+4.65 bps** | +1.01 |
| **Outside** | 9,827 | **+4.23 bps** | +4.16 |
| **Difference (in − out)** | — | **+0.42 bps/day** | Welch t = **+0.09** |

The headline is the opposite of the folklore: in-tournament days earn a *hair more*
than the rest of the tape (+0.42 bps/day), not less — and the gap is statistically
indistinguishable from zero (Welch t = +0.09). The distraction story predicts a
negative gap with a meaningful |t|; we get a microscopic positive gap with |t| ≈ 0.

## The "madness = chaos" corollary — volatility

| Regime | annualised vol |
|---|--:|
| In tournament | **16.8%** |
| Outside | **18.2%** |
| Ratio (in / out) | **0.85** |

Levene equality-of-variance test: stat = 1.10, **p = 0.295**. The tournament window
is, if anything, *slightly calmer* than the rest of the year (vol ratio 0.85, not
>1). No chaos.

## Permutation control (random-placement null)

Draw 5,000 random subsets of 503 trading days (matching the tournament footprint)
and compare each subset's mean to the real in-window mean:

- **pct of random windows with mean ≤ the real in-window mean = 52.9%.**

The real tournament window sits almost exactly at the **median** of the random-null
distribution. There is nothing special about *these* particular days.

## Sub-period stability — the sign flips

| Sub-period | n in-window | in mean | out mean | diff (bps) | Welch t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1985-2004 | 253 | +0.78 bps | +4.71 bps | **−3.93** | −0.61 |
| 2005-2025 | 250 | +8.57 bps | +3.78 bps | **+4.79** | +0.66 |

The in/out gap is **negative** in the first half and **positive** in the second
half, each well inside noise. A real structural effect would not flip sign across
an arbitrary midpoint — this is the signature of a non-effect.

## Could you trade it? — lagged, cost-charged avoidance

Strategy: hold cash during the tournament window, long ^GSPC otherwise, with a
**one-trading-day execution lag** and a **1 bp one-way cost** charged on every
entry/exit (80 switches over 41 years).

| Leg | CAGR |
|---|--:|
| Buy & hold (price-only) | **9.48%** |
| Avoidance, gross | 9.52% |
| Avoidance, net of costs | **9.49%** |
| Excess (net − buy-and-hold) | **+0.02 pp/yr** |

HAC t on the daily net excess return = **−0.10**. The avoidance strategy is a
statistical tie with buy-and-hold: sitting out ~5% of days that happened to be
marginally *positive* on average gives up roughly what it saves, and costs erase
the rest. There is no edge and no vehicle.

## The power reckoning

With ~503 in-window days at ~1.1%/day vol, the standard error on the in-window mean
is ~0.5 bps/day. To clear |t| = 2 the in/out gap would need to be ~1 bp/day (~25
bps over a 3-week window). The observed gap is +0.42 bps/day — and positive. Even a
real distraction drag of a few bps over the whole window would be invisible at this
sample size.

## Positive control (synthetic tape)

Planting a downward tournament drag into the offline synthetic generator and
sweeping its size confirms the machinery is honest:

| Planted drag | in−out diff | Welch t |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 bps/day (null) | +6.5 bps | +1.31 |
| −5 bps/day | +1.5 bps | +0.30 |
| −15 bps/day | −8.5 bps | −1.73 |
| −30 bps/day | −23.5 bps | **−4.77** |

The engine detects a planted drag once it is large enough; the real tape shows
nothing remotely like it (and points the wrong way).

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** In-window mean is +0.42 bps/day *above* the rest of the tape
  (Welch t = +0.09, permutation p = 0.53); the volatility ratio is 0.85 (calmer,
  not chaotic; Levene p = 0.30); the sub-period gap flips sign. No version of the
  distraction claim survives, and the only non-null direction it shows is the
  opposite of the folklore. (Price-only returns; single broad index, so survivorship
  is not a factor.)
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The lagged, cost-charged avoidance strategy ties
  buy-and-hold (+0.02 pp/yr, HAC t = −0.10). There is no vehicle and no edge —
  stepping out of the index for three weeks every March is a coin flip you pay
  commissions to take.
